description: What the 3D view needs to know about an engine that its specification does not already say. Geometry is not here: the renderer derives bore, bank length, layout and propeller size from engine.json, and duplicating cylinder count or displacement in a second file would create two sources of truth for one fact.
type_note: The engine is generated from its specification rather than loaded from a file. An imported model would declare a different type and a model path here; nothing implements that yet, and this field is where it would go so the renderer can branch on it later without being replaced.

turbo.label: TURBO
turbo.title: Turbocharger
turbo.present_when_note: Read from the engine specification. A naturally aspirated engine has no turbocharger, so the component is not built and nothing can be mapped onto it.

channel_components_note: Where a reading is measured, so the view can point at the part a deviation came from. This is instrumentation placement, not a fault table: manifold pressure is read at the induction system whatever has gone wrong. Per-cylinder channels use a wildcard because the index resolves to the cylinder of the same number.
sensor_fault_note: When the diagnosis blames a reading on its own sensor, the probe is marked rather than the cylinder. A dead thermocouple is not a damaged cylinder.
supported_effects_note: Only what the renderer actually does today. state_colour grades a part nominal, caution or warning; outline rings the part the diagnosis is leaning on; probe_suspect marks a distrusted reading in the instrument colour; shake and propeller_unsteadiness are driven by measured vibration health and the speed residual; turbo_spin follows the boost actually being made; stale drops everything to inert grey when telemetry stops.
